currentPackage.name: bounded-scalar-measurement-covariance
scope: experimental dense SourceCovariance matrices for 1 to 64 unique dimensionless scalar source IDs
finite/symmetric/positive-semidefinite validation with relative tolerance in (0, 1e-6], default 1e-12
diagonal variance matching against each used source sigma and J·Σ·Jᵀ scalar propagation
rejects nonzero source sigmas whose squared variance underflows Float rather than treating them as exact
normalizes covariance entries by the largest finite entry before relative-tolerance PSD analysis
uses an underflow-safe midpoint for canonicalization and covariance propagation, including subnormal entries
explicit refusal of covariance for Measurement<Quantity<D>>, Measurement arrays, array reductions and unsupported measurement states
Scientific Lab example, documentation, generated website data and an actual Node WASI Preview 1 smoke entry
preserves original-scale off-diagonal entries for propagation across widely separated covariance magnitudes
uses compensated row and outer sums so large correlated cancellation preserves small residual variance
normalizes stored source contributions by exact powers of two to preserve representable cancellation residuals
builds a scale-safe correlation matrix and applies stored source contributions directly without lossy division and reconstruction
adjusts contributions only when an accepted covariance diagonal differs from the recorded sigma squared
rejects negative and relative-tolerance-unresolved positive factorization pivots instead of changing the covariance result
subnormal source variances compare sqrt(covariance diagonal) against source sigma in root space so rounded subnormal squares cannot accept a materially mismatched diagonal
rejects correlations numerically indistinguishable from perfect dependence instead of rounding away a representable residual variance
reject near-unit unequal-variance correlations unless Float roots reproduce both diagonal values and the geometric product reproduces the covariance entry
explicitly return numerically unresolved for subnormal and normal rounded-geometric-mean precision loss
